construction.copy: the 0x70-byte value built on the stack at rsp+0x20 is copied into obj+0x08..obj+0x78 (seven 16-byte vector moves, via a scratch copy at rsp+0x90)
construction.signature: (out = rsp+0x20, secs in rsi, nanos in rdx, location record pointer in rcx)

conversion.algorithm: exact integer conversion of the f64 to total nanoseconds with round-to-nearest-even, split as (secs, nanos); transcribed band by band in tools/async_duration_step_2f760_115.py and proven equal to the exact rational spec by the model tests

bands.0x3e0 <= exponent < 0x3ff: secs 0, nanos = round-to-nearest-even(value * 1e9) computed on a 128-bit scaled mantissa product; a rounded nanos of exactly 1e9 becomes secs 1, nanos 0
bands.0x3ff <= exponent < 0x433: secs from the mantissa shift, nanos = round-to-nearest-even(fraction * 1e9) with guard/sticky/lsb bits at product bit 51; a rounded nanos of exactly 1e9 carries 1 into secs
bands.0x433 <= exponent < 0x43f: value is already an integer: secs = mantissa << (exponent - 0x433), nanos 0
bands.exponent < 0x3e0: (0, 0): value below 2**-31, including +0.0, -0.0 and positive subnormals

conversion.input: the f64 at obj+0x00, read before anything is written

panics.formatter: 0x1689370 through slot 0x64e13a8; reads the kind byte and writes one of the two messages through the write shim at 0x167fa70 (slot 0x64df720)

kind_0.message: cannot convert float seconds to Duration: value is negative
kind_0.taken_when: the ucomisd comparison 0.0 > value is taken: value negative (including -inf and negative subnormals) or NaN (unordered)

kind_1.message: cannot convert float seconds to Duration: value is either too big or NaN

panics.stack_argument: {pointer to the kind byte on the stack, formatter 0x1689370} at rsp+0x10, passed in rsi; the kind byte itself is stored at rsp+0x0f

dispatch.index: the tag byte at obj+0x78, zero-extended
dispatch.table: 0x938f64, 4-byte signed offsets relative to the table base; the four entries with targets inside this FDE are tags 0..3

false_path.destructor_selection: byte at obj+0x08 == 0 -> 0x5ce86d0 through slot 0x64dfdb8; nonzero -> 0x5ce8da0 through slot 0x64dfdc8
false_path.order: predicate returns false -> counter decrement and conditional destructor -> release call 0x5a52490 with rdi = obj+0x18 -> tag byte at obj+0x78 set to 1 -> return the predicate's 0 in eax
false_path.tag_set_before_release: the tag byte value 1 is loaded into r14b before the release call and stored after it, at the shared exit 0x5a2f9c9

tag_1.shim: 0x1681e60 through slot 0x64e1368, called with rdi = 0x64b81c0; it passes the pre-encoded length 71 (= 2*35 + 1) to the payload builder 0x1680e80

tag_2.shim: 0x1681e80 through slot 0x64e1360, called with rdi = 0x64b81c0; it passes the pre-encoded length 69 (= 2*34 + 1) to the payload builder 0x1680e80; the completion-guard call at 0x5a2f9e8 follows in the byte stream

object_layout.second_argument: rsi at entry, kept in r14 and forwarded unchanged to the predicate
object_layout.tag: +0x78: the dispatch tag byte; the routine writes 3 (predicate true), 1 (predicate false) and 2 (unwind pads) here
object_layout.value_slot: +0x08..+0x78: the 0x70-byte constructed value; inside it, +0x08 of the object is a flag byte selecting the destructor, +0x10 of the object holds the counter pointer, +0x18 of the object is the field the release routine takes

predicate.arguments: (rdi = obj+0x08, rsi = the routine's own second argument)
predicate.false: the false path runs and 0 is returned
predicate.true: tag byte set to 3 at the shared exit, and the predicate's return byte (nonzero) is returned in eax
